observation.reflection:
Verdict: NEEDS_REVISION
Issues: The premise that a lateral CXR is "inherently ambiguous" regarding left/right lung assignment is medically incorrect; lateral views have standard conventions (e.g., the heart shadow is anterior/left, the spine is posterior) that allow for localization, even if difficult. Relying on a third black-box model to "break the tie" introduces more noise and potential bias rather than resolving the anatomical uncertainty. The agent is ignoring the possibility of using geometric/anatomical reasoning or requesting the paired frontal view, which is the gold standard for resolving lateral ambiguities.
Action: Request the paired frontal (PA/AP) chest X-ray to definitively localize the opacity, or apply rule-based anatomical landmark detection (e.g., heart border, diaphragm dome height) on the lateral view instead of consulting another LLM.
